chunks: This is so because you went about exulting wrongfully in the land, and you were insolent.
ai.seo_question: What are the two main reasons for divine punishment mentioned in this verse regarding arrogance and falsehood?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Ghafir is often linked to the fate of Pharaoh's people, illustrating how arrogance (تَمْرَحُونَ) and false joy in worldly power without divine justice (بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِ) lead to spiritual ruin. The term 'tamraḥūna' conveys a sense of frolicsome insolence, emphasizing that their punishment was a direct consequence of their moral decay and rejection of truth. This serves as a timeless warning against the hubris of the oppressor who delights in injustice.
